summary:
MoonSafe is a web-based lunar landing site suitability analysis platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. The project aims to support early-stage assessment of potential landing regions near the Moon's south pole using NASA-derived terrain data.

MoonSafe compares two candidate regions, Shackleton Rim and Malapert Massif, using elevation and slope measurements obtained from lunar terrain datasets. The platform features an interactive dashboard, lunar surface imagery, terrain comparison, landing site safety scoring, and a mission recommendation system.

The application is developed using React, JavaScript, Python, Flask, and Rasterio. Its local backend processes lunar GeoTIFF datasets, while the deployed version uses precomputed terrain statistics to provide accessible online analysis.

MoonSafe makes complex lunar terrain information easier to visualize and compare. It demonstrates how space science data and web technologies can support exploratory mission planning. Future improvements could include solar illumination analysis, communication visibility, and more advanced hazard detection.

MoonSafe is an educational prototype, and its safety scores are not intended for operational landing decisions.
details:
MoonSafe – Lunar Landing Site Safety Analysis

Project Overview

MoonSafe is a web-based lunar landing site suitability analysis platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It helps users compare potential landing regions near the Moon's south pole using NASA-derived terrain data.

How MoonSafe Works

MoonSafe compares two candidate regions: Shackleton Rim and Malapert Massif.

The system uses lunar terrain datasets to examine elevation and slope characteristics. Python and Rasterio are used to process GeoTIFF terrain files and calculate statistics.

The application presents the results through an interactive dashboard with the following features:

  1. Terrain Analysis: Displays elevation and slope measurements for both regions.
  2. Lunar Map: Displays lunar imagery and allows users to select candidate landing regions.
  3. Safety Analysis: Calculates comparative terrain suitability scores.
  4. Mission Recommendation: Identifies a preferred candidate based on the implemented scoring method.
  5. Data Visualization: Makes complex terrain measurements easier to understand.

Technologies Used

  • Frontend: React, JavaScript, Vite, HTML and CSS
  • Backend: Python and Flask
  • Geospatial Processing: Rasterio and NumPy
  • Datasets: NASA-derived lunar elevation and slope GeoTIFF files
  • Deployment: Vercel and Render
  • Version Control: Git and GitHub

Creativity and Innovation

MoonSafe combines scientific terrain measurements with an accessible web interface. Instead of requiring users to examine large geospatial datasets manually, it presents comparative terrain statistics, safety scores, and recommendations in one dashboard.

The online version uses precomputed terrain statistics, enabling users to explore the results without downloading large raster files.

Benefits and Intended Impact

MoonSafe helps students, researchers, and space enthusiasts explore how lunar terrain affects potential landing site selection.

The project demonstrates how publicly available space science data can be transformed into an interactive educational decision-support tool.

Factors Considered

The current prototype considers elevation, slope, and terrain-based suitability. It does not yet include all factors required for real mission planning, such as solar illumination, Earth communication visibility, spacecraft constraints, and detailed landing hazards.

Future Scope

Future improvements include illumination analysis, communication visibility assessment, additional candidate landing regions, and more advanced hazard detection.

Project Links

Live Website: https://moon-safe.vercel.app/

GitHub Repository: https://github.com/alphonsasooter/MoonSafe
